name: TS3USBCA410IRSVR
title: TS3USBCA4 (TS3USBCA410, TS3USBCA420): USB Type-C SBU multiplexer, 3:1 and 4:1, pin or I2C control, UQFN-16
summary: A passive analog multiplexer that links the SBU1/SBU2 contacts of a Type-C receptacle to an audio MIC/AGND pair or to one of two (TS3USBCA410) or three (TS3USBCA420) high-speed pairs for DisplayPort AUX, a PCIe clock or debug. The audio switches are 50 mΩ typ; the high-speed pairs reach about 500 MHz and can be swapped in polarity for plug orientation. Control is by pins or by I2C at one of two addresses, chosen by a three-level strap. It runs from 2.4 V to 5.5 V in a 1.8 mm × 2.6 mm 16-pin UQFN, in commercial (0 °C to 70 °C) and industrial (-40 °C to 85 °C) grades.
key_figures: SEL0/SEL1(/FLIP) pins or I2C up to 400 kHz

notes: An I after the device name marks the industrial range, -40 °C to 85 °C; without it the range is 0 °C to 70 °C. TS3USBCA410 parts are 3:1 multiplexers with a FLIP pin; TS3USBCA420 parts are 4:1 with a third high-speed pair (LnC) in place of FLIP and NC.

circuits.title: TS3USBCA420 in I2C-configuration mode

parts.note: VCC decoupling, close to the pin
VCC decoupling, close to the pin

notes: Misprint: the mux SDA joins the TUSB320 SCL and the mux SCL joins the TUSB320 SDA; it should read SDA to SDA and SCL to SCL.
C1 0.1 µF and C2 1 µF are the recommended VCC decoupling. R1 and R2 take the 0.62 kΩ to 2.2 kΩ range for the SDA and SCL pull-ups; no value is given for R3.
MIC and AGND are swapped for plug orientation by the codec; the audio path of the mux does not swap them.
circuits.description: A smartphone-style Type-C port where the TS3USBCA420 steers the connector's SBU1/SBU2 pair to one of four places: the audio codec's MIC and AGND, a DisplayPort AUX pair, a PCIe clock pair, or a debug pair from the processor. It runs from 3.3 V with I2C_EN tied to the supply, so it answers at ADDR1 on the processor's I2C bus. A TUSB320 on CC1/CC2 shares that bus and has an INT_N line to the processor. A TS5USBA224 switches the D+/D- pins between the USB host and the codec's left and right outputs. OEn is driven by the processor; 0.1 µF and 1 µF decouple VCC.

circuits.description: The same Type-C port with the TS3USBCA420 powered straight from VBUS and I2C_EN left open, so the processor picks the SBU route with SEL0 and SEL1 and gates it with OEn. VCC is decoupled with 0.1 µF and 1 µF.

C1 0.1 µF and C2 1 µF are the recommended VCC decoupling. R1 and R2 take the 0.62 kΩ to 2.2 kΩ range for the SDA and SCL pull-ups; no values are given for R3, R4 and R5.
MIC and AGND are swapped for plug orientation by the codec; the audio path of the mux does not swap them.
circuits.description: A battery-powered Type-C port where the TS3USBCA410 sends SBU1/SBU2 to the codec's MIC and AGND, a DisplayPort AUX pair, or a debug pair from the processor. VCC comes from VBAT; a resistor divider from VBAT to ground holds I2C_EN at mid level, so the part answers at ADDR0 and the processor sets SWSEL and FLIPSEL over I2C. A TUSB320 on CC1/CC2 shares the bus and has an INT_N line to the processor. FLIP is unused in this mode. A TS5USBA224 shares the D+/D- pins between the USB host and the codec's left and right outputs.

circuits.description: The TS3USBCA410 run from VBUS with I2C_EN open: the processor chooses the route with SEL0 and SEL1, sets the plug orientation on FLIP and enables the switch with OEn. A TUSB322I on CC1/CC2 has ID, DIR and OUT3 lines to the processor, each pulled up to the processor's I/O rail. SBU1/SBU2 go to the codec's MIC and AGND, a DisplayPort AUX pair, or a debug pair. VCC is decoupled with 0.1 µF and 1 µF.

circuits.title: ON-state resistance test, audio path (RON_AGND)
circuits.description: SEL0 high and SEL1 low select the MIC_GND path. VIN1 and VIN2 hold SBU1 and SBU2 at 0 V while current sinks IO1 and IO2 pull 75 mA out of MIC_GND1 and MIC_GND2; each path's resistance is VIN/IO. The six high-speed pins end in 50 Ω.

circuits.title: ON-state resistance test, high-speed path (RON_HS)
circuits.description: SEL0 and SEL1 both high select the LnA pair. VIN1 and VIN2 hold SBU1 and SBU2 at 3.3 V; IO1 draws 40 mA from LnAp and IO2 -40 mA from LnAn, and RON is VIN/IO. MIC_GND1 sits on a 1.5 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V with 50 pF to ground, MIC_GND2 is grounded, and the LnB and LnC pins end in 50 Ω.

circuits.title: ON- and OFF-state capacitance test, high-speed path (CON_HS, COFF_HS)
circuits.description: Network-analyzer ports 1 and 2 (50 Ω) connect to LnAp and LnAn; SEL0 and SEL1 high select that pair. The differential impedance from SDD11 at 500 MHz gives the capacitance. SBU and MIC_GND pins are left open; LnB and LnC end in 50 Ω.

circuits.title: Power supply rejection test (PSR)
circuits.description: A DC supply feeds VCC through resistor R, and an arbitrary waveform generator adds 400 mVpp at 217 Hz, 1 kHz or 20 kHz through C1, so VCC is 3.3 V ± 200 mVpp. The audio path is selected (SEL0 high, SEL1 low); MIC_GND1 reaches a spectrum analyzer's 50 Ω input through C2 and MIC_GND2 is grounded. PSR = 20 log(VO/VN).

circuits.title: Total harmonic distortion test (THD)
circuits.description: An audio analyzer's generator drives SBU1 through RS = 600 Ω, and MIC_GND1 returns to the analyzer's 600 Ω load; MIC_GND2 is grounded and SBU2 open. SEL0 high and SEL1 low select the audio path.
notes: RS and RL7 are inside the audio analyzer.

circuits.title: Crosstalk test between MIC and AGND (XTALK_MICGND)
circuits.description: A four-port network analyzer (50 Ω) connects port 1 to SBU1, port 2 to SBU2, port 3 to MIC_GND1 and port 4 to MIC_GND2, with the audio path selected (SEL0 high, SEL1 low). Crosstalk is S43. The high-speed pins end in 50 Ω.

circuits.title: OFF isolation test (ISOOFF_MICGND)
circuits.description: The same four-port connection with SEL0, SEL1 and I2C_EN left open, so the audio path is off. ISOOFF_MICGND1 is S31 and ISOOFF_MICGND2 is S42. The high-speed pins end in 50 Ω.

circuits.title: Turn-on and turn-off time test, audio path (tON_MICGND, tOFF_MICGND)
circuits.description: VS1 holds SBU1 at 3.3 V and VS2 holds SBU2 at 0 V. MIC_GND1 is the output VO, pulled up to 1.8 V through 2.1 kΩ with 50 pF to ground; MIC_GND2 is grounded. SEL[1:0] steps between 0 V and 3.3 V; tON is from the 50 % point of that step to VO reaching 90 %, tOFF to VO falling to 10 %.

circuits.title: Turn-on and turn-off time test, high-speed path (tON_HS, tOFF_HS)
circuits.description: Two 50 Ω sources drive SBU1 (VS1 = 3.3 V) and SBU2 (VS2 = 0 V). The outputs VO1 and VO2 are LnBp and LnBn, each ending in 50 Ω. MIC_GND1 carries the 1.8 V / 2.1 kΩ / 50 pF load and MIC_GND2 goes to ground through a switch. SEL[1:0] steps between its levels; tON is from its 50 % point to VO1 at 90 %, tOFF to VO1 at 10 %.

circuits.title: Break-before-make time test (tBBM)
circuits.description: VS1 holds SBU1 at 3.3 V and VS2 holds SBU2 at 0 V. LnBp (VO1) ends in 50 Ω, and MIC_GND1 (VO) carries the 1.8 V / 2.1 kΩ / 50 pF load; MIC_GND2 goes to ground through a switch. When SEL[1:0] changes from the LnB route to the audio route, tBBM is the gap from VO1 falling to 10 % to VO rising past 10 %.

equations.name: Audio-path ON resistance
equations.expr: RON_AGND1 = VIN1 / IO1;  RON_AGND2 = VIN2 / IO2

where.VIN1, VIN2: voltage forced on SBU1, SBU2 (0 V)
where.IO1, IO2: current drawn from MIC_GND1, MIC_GND2 (75 mA)

equations.name: High-speed ON resistance
equations.expr: RON_HS1 = VIN1 / IO1;  RON_HS2 = VIN2 / IO2

where.IO1, IO2: current at LnAp (40 mA) and LnAn (-40 mA)

where.SDD11: differential return loss measured at the LnA pair

operation.text: A passive analog switch for the SBU1 and SBU2 contacts of a Type-C receptacle. The TS3USBCA420 routes SBU1/SBU2 to one of four pin pairs, the TS3USBCA410 to one of three: an audio MIC/AGND pair and two or three high-speed pairs suited to DisplayPort AUX, a PCIe clock, debug, UART or I2C. Both run from 2.4 V to 5.5 V, so VBUS, a one-cell battery or a regulated rail can supply them.

SBU1 and SBU2 connect to MIC_GND1 and MIC_GND2 through two identical very-low-resistance switches (50 mΩ typ), giving low THD and low MIC-to-AGND crosstalk. The audio path cannot swap MIC and AGND; that swap is left to the codec.

Three pairs on the TS3USBCA420 (LnA, LnB, LnC) and two on the TS3USBCA410 (LnA, LnB), all alike: about 500 MHz bandwidth, a few ohms of ON resistance and low added jitter. Each pair's polarity can be reversed for plug orientation, over I2C on the TS3USBCA420 and over I2C or the FLIP pin on the TS3USBCA410. Switching between routes is break-before-make.

I2C_EN is a three-level strap. Grounded or open (L) gives pin-configuration mode, where SEL0, SEL1 and, on the TS3USBCA410, FLIP set the route. At VCC/2 (M) or VCC (H) the part is in I2C mode at address ADDR0 or ADDR1 respectively, and the SEL pins become SDA and SCL.

OEn high holds the part in reset with bandgap and I/O buffers off, I2C dead and the registers cleared; it is the default through the internal pull-up. With OEn low, the DEVICE_ENABLE bit (General_1 bit 1) turns the switch on; with that bit at 0 the switch is off but I2C still works. Unselected ports are high impedance.

VCC must ramp from 0 to 100 % in 0.1 ms to 100 ms. After VCC passes its minimum, an internal power-good rises within tD_PG (250 µs max); the SEL0, SEL1 and I2C_EN levels are debounced for tCFG_DB. Device ready follows OEn low within tDEV_ENABLE. Keeping VCC rise and fall within these limits makes the power-on reset trip reliably.

The controller sends START, the 7-bit address with W/R = 0, and after the acknowledge one register sub-address byte, MSB first, then one or more data bytes, each acknowledged, and STOP. Setting a read start address is the same transfer stopped after the sub-address.

After START and the address with W/R = 1, the part returns register bytes MSB first, starting at the sub-address of the last write, or else at 00h or one past the last register read. It keeps sending while the controller acknowledges each byte; the controller ends with STOP. The sub-address is 0x00 after reset and steps by one after every completed transfer.

Any source in 2.4 V to 5.5 V works. A regulated 3.3 V keeps performance tighter than a cell swinging 2.7 V to 4.3 V, at some cost in parts and board area. Parametric drift with supply, the supply ranges of neighbouring parts and their I/O levels all bear on the choice.

I2C mode needs fewer processor pins and is preferred; on the TS3USBCA420 it is also the only way to flip the high-speed pairs. The two addresses, picked by the I2C_EN strap, avoid clashes on a shared bus. The control inputs have defined VIH and VIL for a wide range of logic levels, but compatibility with the processor's I/O must be checked and a level translator added if needed.

For address ADDR0, I2C_EN is held at mid level by a divider. Large resistors keep its standing current low, but the resistor tolerance and the internal pull-down (1.6 MΩ to 5.8 MΩ) must still leave the pin inside the VIML to VIMH window.

operation.topic: High-speed bandwidth and the audio port
operation.text: The high-speed bandwidth figure assumes the audio port is open. The low-resistance audio switch puts a large capacitance between MIC_GND pins and SBU pins, so any load or trace on the audio port can cut the high-speed bandwidth sharply. Where bandwidth matters most, the audio channel is the better route; signals that must use a high-speed lane need a lightly loaded audio port.
The maximum supported current falls as contact resistance rises: about 250 mA at 20 mΩ, 100 mA at 50 mΩ and 50 mA at 100 mΩ.
Decouple VCC to ground with 0.1 µF and 1 µF, both as close to the part as possible.

Keep the decoupling capacitors next to VCC. Keep the total resistance between the connector's SBU pins and the codec's MIC and AGND pins low, since series resistance worsens crosstalk. Route I2C and other digital lines away from the audio lines. In the TS3USBCA420 layout, VCC and GND reach their planes through vias beside the pins.

packages.name: UQFN-16 (RSV0016A), 1.8 mm × 2.6 mm, 0.4 mm pitch

at MMC to C A B; 0.05 at MMC
notes: Pins 1-4 run down one long side and 9-12 up the other; pins 5-8 and 13-16 sit on the short sides. There is no exposed pad.

Land pattern: pads (0.2) wide at (0.4) pitch, (0.6) long (pin 1 pad (0.7)), pad-row centres (2.4) and (1.6) apart, corner radius (R0.05); non-solder-mask-defined pads (preferred) with mask opening 0.05 max all around, or solder-mask-defined pads with 0.05 min metal under the mask all around. The stencil uses the same apertures in a 0.125 mm sheet.
